correctness.rationale: Direct matrix identities (M^7, M^28), determinant-one cyclicity, exact order lifting, unique scalar root lifting in residues 4 and 6 modulo seven, and the 2-adic logarithm with two odd initial normalized coefficients establish the unrestricted claim. The unit divided difference yields an exact two-root valuation formula on 28t, and each root branch has four representatives. An extracted standalone integer verifier corroborates all identities and cycles k<=13; finite tests alone are not a proof.

originality.rationale: The new scalar eleven-zero census and local two-root valuation identity are not implied by the inspected prime-power period theorem (Kuloğlu 2022, Theorem 2.5) or by the 3-adic results of Guadalupe and Ismail et al. Sobolewski 2017 covers even-order consecutive-step recurrences rather than this lacunary order-three recurrence. Targeted published-finding corpus, web and own-claim checks found no equivalent record; priority remains limited to inspected materials.
residual_risks: A relevant unindexed paper or implicit corollary of a general third-order recurrence valuation theorem might cover the eleven-root classification.
The generic prime-power period-growth result is pre-existing; novelty is not asserted for that method.
The arXiv 2021 3-adic paper was compared through abstract/metadata rather than line-by-line complete PDF.

value.rationale: A precise infinite 2-adic zero-spectrum/density for a natural third-order recurrence answers an intrinsic divisibility question. The unusual persistent count eleven is explained by a nontrivial two-root 2-adic analytic factorization plus three simple branches, and the 28t valuation identity supports future arithmetic analysis. It is neither an isolated small modulus nor a routine finite table recomputation.
